subject: Pricing & batching follow-up — token volumes and continuous batching assumptions
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & asks — token volumes, target $/1M, batching expectations

Thanks again for taking the call today, Sophie — really helpful to understand Acme AI's roadmap and traffic patterns. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored pricing estimate and recommendation: 

1) Traffic profile (what we heard today)
   - Primary workload: low-latency multi-turn chat for customer support + a background summarization job.
   - Expected monthly tokens: rough band 50M–120M initially (you mentioned growth into the 100s within 6–12 months).
   - Typical response size today: ~30–80 tokens; summarization jobs are 500–2,000 tokens/sample.

2) Key commercial targets / constraints
   - Target unit economics: you mentioned a target in the ballpark of $150–$250 per 1M tokens (is that correct?). Please confirm target $/1M.
   - Budget range for inference (monthly): you indicated $8k–$20k to start. Confirm if that’s committed or target.

3) Batching & concurrency assumptions we need to validate
   - Chat workload: mostly continuous traffic with a fairly steady QPS (not huge spikes), low single-digit second latency SLO.
   - Continuous batching: are you expecting requests to be streamed continuously such that we can rely on sustained effective batching versus bursty arrival? If so, what is the average requests/sec and your acceptable tail latency (P95/P99)?
   - Concurrency: any hard limits on concurrent sessions/open connections?

Next steps / asks for you (Sophie/Jordan)
   - Please confirm target $/1M tokens and the monthly budget band.
   - Share a sample traffic export (CSV) with timestamped request sizes if possible — that lets us model batching gains and give a tighter $/1M estimate.

We’ll produce a preliminary pricing estimate + recommended serving configuration (hosted vs dedicated, batching window, concurrency targets) once we have the sample data. Attached is a high-level pricing template we’ll fill in (redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf).

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

---
Attachment: redwood-pricing-estimate.pdf (pdf, 42KB)
From: Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@acmeai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmeai.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & asks — token volumes, target $/1M, batching expectations

Thanks Camila — great summary. Quick answers below and we’ll upload a sample CSV by end of week.

- Target $/1M tokens: yes, our stretch target is $150/1M but we’d be comfortable up to $200/1M if latency and availability are solid. Anything above $250/1M is tough.
- Budget: initial monthly spend target $10k–$15k for the next 90 days; expecting to ramp to $30k+/month over the next 6–12 months if the pilot goes well.
- Monthly volume: roughly 50M tokens/month right now across chat + summarization. We have a growth plan to 120M tokens/month within 6 months if conversion increases.

Workload characteristics (more detail):
- Chat: continuous traffic across US region, steady-state ~40 QPS during business hours, peak ~120 QPS for brief periods. Average tokens per chat response ~45. We need P95 latency < 800ms for first token.
- Summarization: batch jobs run every hour; each job processes ~2k documents for summarization with average response token 800–1,200. Latency for summarization can be higher (seconds), but throughput matters.
- Concurrency: we expect 200–400 concurrent sessions at peak. We don’t want connection limits to surface at the application level.

Continuous batching: we do expect a steady stream for chat (i.e., continuous batching should be effective). For summarization, batching is job-based and can be optimized separately.

I’ll attach a stripped-down usage sample now (acme-usage-sample.csv) and follow up with a fuller export. Happy to hop on a quick 20-min call to walk through if helpful.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Liu
Head of Product, Acme AI
sophie.liu@acmeai.com

---
Attachment: acme-usage-sample.csv (csv, 18KB)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Liu <sophie.liu@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & asks — token volumes, target $/1M, batching expectations

Appreciate the details, Sophie — that’s exactly what we need. A few clarifying items so our cost model matches your expectations:

1) Target $/1M: confirmed you’re aiming for $150–$200 as a practical range. We’ll model both 150 and 200 to show the delta.
2) Continuous batching assumptions:
   - For chat: because you have steady traffic (~40 QPS steady, bursts to 120 QPS), we’ll assume continuous batching with an adaptive window. Practically that means we’ll use micro-batching (10–50ms target enqueue windows) and dynamic batch sizing to preserve first-token latency while improving token throughput.
   - We’ll model expected batching efficiency as a percentage reduction in per-token cost — with your steady traffic we’d expect 20–35% savings vs naïve single-request serving. I’ll include a sensitivity table.
3) Concurrency/throughput: we’ll recommend a 2-stage approach:
   - Pilot on hosted (shared) with aggressive batching and prefix cache to hit the $150–200 range at your current volumes.
   - If you hit the higher volume ranges (100M+ tokens/month) or need tighter SLOs, Dedicated capacity significantly lowers unit cost — we’ll include a dedicated-case model.

Action items for us:
- I’ll fill the pricing template for both hosted and dedicated scenarios (attached).
- Marissa (cc’d) will run some quick sims against your CSV to validate the 20–35% batching lift.

Would you be available next Tue (7/1) 10am PT for a 20-min follow-up to review the draft estimates?

Thanks — Camila

Subject: Re: Pricing & batching follow-up — quick sims and notes

Quick note from infra side: we ran a small sim against the sample CSV Sophie shared. Preliminary findings: with continuous batching and adaptive micro-windows we saw ~28% reduction in per-token compute cost for the chat mix (45 tokens/response average). Summarization jobs benefit more from larger batch sizes but with higher memory footprint — we’ll include memory + GPU sizing in the detailed estimate.

Also tagging that if Acme is ok exploring Dedicated, we can push unit costs below the $150/1M token target at 100M+ monthly volumes (will outline thresholds in the doc).

-Marissa
